rawOutput.rationale: This is a problem-solving plan for learning the product rule from scratch. Four short sessions fit the available 15-minute windows. The sequence begins with one complete example and one visible step at a time, then moves to guided use, independent application, and mixed verification. Knowledge-map topics were not supplied, so session topicIds remain empty.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build the product rule from the structure of two multiplied functions.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule model and one complete worked derivative
contentTargets: Recognize when a function is a product of two differentiable factors
Interpret and apply (fg)' = f'g + fg'
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating each factor and multiplying the results is incorrect
Apply the product rule to one example with both factors identified

sessions.title: Use the Rule with Guidance
sessions.objective: Carry out the product-rule procedure accurately on a similar expression.
sessions.amountLabel: Two guided derivatives with power-rule factors
contentTargets: Differentiate each factor using the power rule
Assemble and simplify a product-rule derivative
completionEvidence: Solve one product-rule derivative with step prompts
Explain where each term in the derivative comes from

sessions.title: Apply the Product Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Choose and execute the product rule without procedural prompts.
contentTargets: Select the product rule when multiplication joins two nonconstant factors
Produce and check an independent solution
completionEvidence: Solve two product-rule derivatives without step prompts
Compare each result with a structured rule check and correct any error

sessions.title: Verify Flexible Use
sessions.objective: Distinguish product-rule problems and apply the rule accurately in mixed practice.
sessions.amountLabel: Three mixed classifications and two derivative solutions
contentTargets: Distinguish products from expressions requiring only the power rule
Apply the product rule independently in mixed practice
completionEvidence: Classify three expressions by the differentiation rule required
Solve two selected derivatives and explain the rule choice

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate model, explain the idea in your own words, repair any gap, and explain it again without copying.

how: State the idea in your own words.
Compare your attempt with the model and fix the gap.

personalization: Use the concrete example style you prefer.

activities.label: Recognize a product structure
activities.title: Product structure first
activities.body: Look at the model and note the two factors. Then identify what makes this a product.

essentialIdeas: An expression is a product of two differentiable factors when it is written as two differentiable functions multiplied together, so the product structure must be recognized before,

activities.label: Say it in your own words
activities.title: Your own product check
activities.body: Explain whether the expression is a product and name its two factors. Keep it brief.
activities.concept: Recognize whether an expression is a product of two differentiable factors
activities.correctAnswer: It is a product of two differentiable factors because it is written as two differentiable functions multiplied together; the two factors are the separate functions in the expression.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names the product structure and the two factors. If the factors are not separated, repair that first.

activities.label: Fix the recognition gap
activities.title: Repair the product check
activities.body: Revise your answer using the model. State the product structure and the two factors again.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Thinking the whole expression should be treated as one piece instead of noticing the two multiplied differentiable factors.
activities.concept: Recognize whether an expression is a product of two differentiable factors
activities.correctAnswer: The expression is a product because it consists of two differentiable factors multiplied together; the factors are the two separate functions.
activities.feedback: The key repair is to separate the expression into two differentiable factors. That recognition is what matters here.

activities.label: Explain it again clearly
activities.title: Explain the structure again
activities.body: Explain the recognition in one or two sentences without copying the model. Use the factors directly.
activities.concept: Recognize whether an expression is a product of two differentiable factors
activities.correctAnswer: A product-rule situation appears when one expression is the multiplication of two differentiable factors, so you first identify the two factors before doing anything else.
activities.feedback: Good if you clearly state the product structure and the two factors. Keep the explanation plain and direct.

activities.label: Recognize the setup
activities.title: Which setup needs a product rule?
activities.body: Choose the expression that is a product of two differentiable factors.
activities.concept: Recognize when a function is a product of two differentiable factors
choices: The expression written as two differentiable functions multiplied together
An expression with only one differentiable factor
An expression that is a single differentiable function
An expression that is a constant number only
activities.correctAnswer: The expression written as two differentiable functions multiplied together
activities.feedback: The product rule applies when you can see two differentiable factors being multiplied. The other choices do not show that product structure.
